description.narrative: The development objective of the Higher Education Project for Tajikistan is to develop mechanisms that improve and monitor the quality and labor market relevance of higher education. The project comprises of three components. The first component, institutional-level improvements consists of following two sub-components: (i) just-in-time grants to re- and up-skill workforce; and (ii) competitive grant program for universities. The second component, system-level interventions consists of following three sub-components: (i) quality assurance enhancements; (ii) system-wide higher education curriculum reform; and (iii) assessment of higher education financing. The third component will support project management, communication, training, monitoring and evaluation, operating costs, and the project's audits.
The objective of the project is to develop mechanisms that improve and monitor the quality and labor-market relevance of higher education

title.narrative: Percentage of peer reviewed CGP sub-grants that are assessed to have improved the quality and relevance of the targeted program

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. A Peer Review of the CGP subprojects implementation found that 100 percent of CGP subprojects have improved the quality and relevance of the targeted programs, exceeding the target of 65 percent. Of these, 77 percent of subprojects were rated by the peer reviewers as “highly successful” and 23 percent were rated as “successful”. </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of HEIs conducting graduate tracing surveys to monitor employment outcomes of alumni

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. The third round of GTS covered graduates in all 34 eligible HEIs or 100 percent of HEIs.</p>

title.narrative: MoES responds and/or resolves the grievance received within the stipulated service standard for response times

comment.narrative: <p>The GRM was established and functioning. According to MOES no claims were received. During the implementation support missions, the Bank team did not receive any complaint. </p>

title.narrative: Number of working groups established to revise curriculum for selected clusters of academic specialties

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. In addition to 15 working groups (vs. 5 planned) established to revise curriculum for selected clusters of academic specialties 62 working groups were established for specialties beyond the selected clusters.</p>

title.narrative: Number of HEIs that complete a pilot institutional accreditation process in accordance with the newly developed accreditation standards and guidelines

comment.narrative: <p>Target is achieved. The pilot in three universities was completed in December 2020 (with over 6 months delay due to the pandemic). The accreditation reports have been prepared. New standards and guidelines have been developed and approved by ASSES. </p>
<p>Target is surpassed. Direct project beneficiaries are 30,800 in total (vs. 15,250 planned) including 3,300 HEIs teachers and professors, and 27,500 students.</p>

title.narrative: Number of students enrolled in short-term offerings (courses or programs) developed in response to labor market demand

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. Under 21 small sub-projects, Just-in-Time grants program provided training to 3,499 persons (including returning migrants and secondary education graduates entering the labor market with limited work experience), including 2,009 women who received skills and competencies consistent with labor market needs.</p>

title.narrative: Number of CGP sub-projects that engage employers to implement at least one strategic initiative focused on improving relevance

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. Under both CGP windows, 38 sub-projects (vs. 30 planned) engaged 80 employers in revising curriculum, arranging internships, inviting employer lectures, creating centers for innovative technologies, career development, etc. to improve the relevance of their academic programs to respond to labor market demand.</p>

title.narrative: Number of female students receiving custom academic and student support services

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. Female students have been provided with support in preparing for admission to HEIs, their graduation and subsequent transition to work, including the implementation of a program to create living conditions and career development centers, mentoring programs, a series of lectures and master classes on gender and personal development.</p>

title.narrative: Number of clusters of academic specialties with standards revised utilizing a process that incorporates employer feedback

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. Curriculum was revised for selected specialties from 7 academic clusters of high demand by the labor marketand for which working groups were established: Pedagogy; Economics and Statistics; Finance, Credit and Accounting; Business administration and management; Tourism, Energy, Construction. The revision was supported by international partners and incorporated the feedback of employers and local experts. </p>

title.narrative: Assessment of higher education financing completed and recommendations for a more effective and performance-orientated allocation developed.

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator is revised at the restructuring. The revised target is achieved.</p>

actual.value: The assessment has been conducted and report with recommendations has been produced

title.narrative: New quality assurance standards and guidelines, aligned with Bologna Process, for institutional accreditation are developed, piloted , and approved by the government

baseline.value: Standards and guidelines not aligned with Bologna Process.

comment.narrative: <p>Target is achieved. New standards and guidelines (the Guideline) were developed with support from Estonian Quality Assurance (QA) Agency EKKA which is an internationally certified member of the European Association for QA in Higher Education (HE) (formerly, the European Network for QA in HE - ENQA). The Guideline was approved by ASSES, the government authorized body in QA in HE in Tajikistan, following the new institutional accreditation pilot and wide consultations with the stakeholders.</p>

actual.value: New standards and guidelines approved by ASSES

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning
Number of NGOs involved in planning and implementation of project-related activities

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. To support female students, 7 NGOs (vs. 3 planned) have been engaged to participate in the planning and implementation of activities related to research, developing a mechanism to motivate girls to attend HE, organizing and conducting seminars and trainings on gender issues, personal and professional growth and organizing meetings with employers.</p>

title.narrative: Higher Education Institutions receiving labs and information technology equipment

comment.narrative: <p>Target is surpassed. New indicator added at the restructuring. In all, 77 percent of HEIs (30 HEIs out of 39 total) received labs and information technology equipment to improve quality of their learning environment and teaching. </p>
